symptom: Node 22.16.0 synthetic reproduction showed that a no-op Object.freeze leaves validation verdict objects and their error lists mutable. Source inspection of v0.1 found frozenValidation using the live Object.freeze method, so a caller could alter a previously issued invalid verdict or its diagnostics after validation. This is a research-only integrity issue; no private K evidence, N2 activation, production data or observed attack was involved.
lesson: Validation result immutability is not guaranteed by calling Object.freeze if the reference is looked up from the mutable caller realm at validation time. A previously issued fail-closed verdict can be relabeled or its diagnostic evidence altered.
guardrail: Capture native Object.freeze at module initialization and use the captured method for both validation errors and verdict envelope. Under reversible synthetic no-op Object.freeze replacement, assert valid and malformed results preserve frozen verdict and diagnostic arrays and reject attempted mutation. This does not establish issuer rights, finality, scoring or production authority.
